Subject: ACME post-call TCO recap & next steps (cost-focused)

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the cost levers we discussed so your team can review and share with Finance: 

Key pain points (what you told us)
- High inference spend driven by ~120M tokens/month across chat and async generation.
- Tight budget envelope for inference: target ~$25k/month for production usage.
- Need to keep latency under 300ms p95 for chat and maintain model quality for customer-facing flows.

What we recommend (cost/TCO levers we can apply)
1) Batching & concurrency tuning: For your mostly short prompts (avg 150 tokens), batching to an average batch size of 6–8 can reduce GPU utilization by ~30–40% in our tests while keeping tail latency under target for most traffic patterns.
2) Prefix/KV caching for repetitive contexts: ~45% of your requests have long, repeating system prompts — prefix caching can cut per-request compute by ~20–35% depending on hit rate.
3) Quantization model variant: switching to a 4-bit quantized variant for non-sensitive flows can reduce cost per token by ~25–35% with negligible quality delta on most instruction prompts.
4) Routing & fallbacks: Route lower-cost batchable workloads to a cheaper model variant and keep the high-quality variant for low-latency chat. This hybrid routing gives ~20% blended saving.

Ballpark TCO (very approximate — included workbook has scenarios):
- Current estimated baseline (your reported usage): 120M tokens/month -> estimated infra cost approx $48k/mo (baseline model variant, no caching/batching).
- Combined levers (batching, caching, quantized variants, routing): expected 55–65% reduction -> target run rate approx $17–22k/mo. That brings you into the stated budget envelope when combined with a small committed discount.

Attachments: I attached a TCO workbook (ACME_Redwood_TCO_Workbook_v1.xlsx) with three scenarios (baseline, conservative savings, aggressive savings) and assumptions so Finance can validate. Also included a one-pager (redwood_tco_onepager.pdf) summarizing the levers and rough ROI.

Next steps / owners
- Marissa (me): send TCO workbook (attached) — done.
- Rafael (cc): will run a quick dedicated-cost scenario with Dedicated pricing and a 30-day pilot option (Rafael to deliver by Wed).
- Samantha / Tom: share procurement contact and current committed vendor process; confirm whether Acme can trial a 30-day pilot with a $10k commit or needs a different procurement approach.
- Schedule: proposed technical deep-dive with your infra team to validate caching hits and token distribution — suggest Wed 3/17 or Thu 3/18.

Open questions I captured
- What % of requests are low-sensitivity (can use quantized variants)?
- Can you share a token histogram or sample distribution for chat vs async? That will help refine batching profile.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the workbook live.

Best,
